summary: James Blumenthal was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and held posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College (attested 2013-2015).

James Burgess worked in Indian history and archaeology. Educated at the universities of Glasgow and Edinburgh, he served as Director and later Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1886-1889) and founded Indian Antiquary and Epigraphia Indica.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975-2013).

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015-2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist. He studied at the East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and later served as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault and Michel Bréal at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, later holding posts there (~1877-1894) and at the Collège de France (1885-1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961-1964) under Sheldon Pollock and served at the University of Iowa (~1971-2015), where he became Professor Emeritus.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College (~1830-1833). He held a post at Yale University from circa 1850 to 1892, where he taught Charles Rockwell Lanman.

James Fergusson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.
James Fieser is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University, and held a post at the University of Tennessee around 1992.
James G. Mullens specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James H. Austin is a neurologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under teachers including Nanrei Sohaku Kobori. He held academic posts at the University of Oregon (~1956-1965) and the University of Colorado (~1965-1992).

James Hadley worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Yale College and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury. He served as Professor of Greek at Yale University (1845-1872) and as a leading member of the American Oriental Society (1871-1872).

James Haughton Woods was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, and Charles Rockwell Lanman, later holding a post at Harvard University (~1903-1935).

James Irving Manatt was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, later holding posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Brown University (~1892-1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sonoma State University and the Pacific School of Religion, and founded Boundless Way Zen and the Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004-2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

James L. Taylor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and anthropology. He earned his PhD at Macquarie University in 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).
James Legge was a sinologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1831-1835) and Highbury College. He served as Professor at the University of Oxford beginning in 1876.
